newsitem.title: TURKEY: TURK FACTORING-LEASING SECTOR HAS LOWEST P/E IN MAY.
newsitem.headline: TURK FACTORING-LEASING SECTOR HAS LOWEST P/E IN MAY.

text.p: Seven Turkish factoring and leasing firms listed on the Istanbul Stock Exchange had the lowest price/earning (p/e) ratio with a sector average of 4.45 on May 23, down from 5.86 at end-1996, according to data released by the Exchange.
The data showed the most expensive sector as transportation with three listed companies which have a 42.10 percent average p/e ratio on May 23, after 44.27 percent at the end of 1996.
Oz Finans Factoring had the lowest p/e ratio in the leasing-factoring sector with 2.69 on May 23, followed by Vakf Leasing with 3.47 and Iktisat Leasing with 3.88.
The data showed that Turkish Airlines led the way in the transportation sector with 68.28 p/e ratio on May 23, compared to 63.83 at the end of 1996.
Oz Finans Faktoring raised its net profits by 36 percent to 69.56 billion in the first quarter of 1996, compared to a year ago. THY has not yet released its first quarter results.
The leasing-factoring sector was followed by paper, printing and publishing industry with an average p/e ratio of 7.42 and forestry-furniture industry with 7.71 on May 23.
Besides the industrial, services and financial sectors, 17 listed investment trusts had an average p/e ratio of 3.16 on May 23.
